title: Samsung's second Taylor chip plant to begin construction next month
key_facts: Construction on Samsung's second plant in Taylor, Texas, begins next month.

Jon Taylor, Samsung vice president of infra technology and leader of its Austin and Taylor sites, said the first plant is 'still on track' to be online by end of the year, about five years after the $17 billion project was announced.
The first plant will use 2-nanometer technology, the first in the US; it is in a lengthy qualification phase for tools, factory and product.
Tesla is the only officially named customer, with a $16.5 billion deal for AI chips; Taylor said Musk's Terafab plans do not change that deal.
Samsung could build up to 10 plants on 1,200+ acres; its first plant was delayed by supply chain issues and reported struggles to find customers.
Samsung also announced $22.8 million in community and workforce investments.
quote_evidence: "The world is looking at Taylor for the chips that will power the future, and we aren't stopping just at one fab," Taylor said.
The first facility was initially expected to be near full completion by the end of 2025, but its completion was delayed due to supply chain issues and reported struggles to nail down customers.
why_it_matters_hint: More US chipmaking capacity in Texas, though customers beyond Tesla are unnamed.
